results.evidence: Nobody climbs Crowder on its own trip, and no source gives a car-to-car gain for a Crowder-only outing. The only documented ascents are inside long enchainments (e.g. a 7-day Mystery Ridge-to-Northern Pickets enchainment totalling 55 mi / 38,900 ft gain), and those cannot settle this route's figure. gain_ft 6,582 looks like the net trailhead-to-summit difference. The itinerary's 13,980 ft sum rests on a day plan that is itself doubtful: it descends to Pickell Pass on day 4, then retraces over Wild Pass on day 5. No patch without two agreeing sources.

The page shows dist_km (61.15 km = 38 mi) as the ONE-WAY approach, which is not plausible. But no source gives a one-way distance for a Crowder-only approach from Goodell Creek or Ross Lake. Published figures are for multi-peak traverses (55-66 mi totals). The correct one-way value cannot be established from two sources.

results.correct_value: The approach row should describe the off-trail traverse to Wild Pass/Wild Lake and the Phantom-Crowder col, as the approach text, waypoints and itinerary all do.
results.evidence: The Baker River -> Ruth/Icy/Mineral -> Easy Peak -> Perfect Pass line is the start of a Baker Lake-to-Ross Lake traverse. That party did NOT summit Crowder: they bailed before the Crowder Bypass and went toward Luna Col, so this is not the route's approach. An enchainment that did climb Crowder came from Pioneer Peak down to Wild Pass/Wild Lake, then up the easy SW Flank. That matches the row's approach text, the Wild Pass and Phantom-Crowder col waypoints, and the itinerary: 4+ fields against the one outlier.

results.fact: CAMPING & BIVY list does not match this route's own camps
results.evidence: The bivy array is the regional Northern Pickets/Challenger camp list: Luna Camp, Beaver Pass, Luna Col, Perfect Pass, Whatcom Camp, Twin Rocks/Stillwell, Challenger Arm, Wiley Ridge benches, Easy Ridge, Tapto Lakes, Luna Cirque. Only the Big Beaver trail camps (Luna Camp, Beaver Pass) plausibly serve the northern/eastern Big Beaver entry named in the approach. The rest serve Challenger/Whatcom/Luna/Fury, not Crowder. The route's own camps (Terror Basin, Wild Pass/Wild Lake, Pickell Pass) are missing. Handled as a catalog-wide class; no patch.

results.fact: ROUTE BREAKDOWN 'Crowder Bypass' row and beta treat a traverse bypass as part of the SW Flank climb
results.evidence: pitch_detail[1] ('Crowder Bypass': steep snow/trees/gullies, 'no real alternative') and beta ('Once through ... the infamous Crowder Bypass') come from a through-traverse that passes Crowder on its west side, and that party never climbed Crowder. The approach text, waypoints and itinerary reach the SW Flank via Wild Pass and never mention a bypass. Only one source describes the bypass, and it does not show whether the bypass lies on the way to Crowder's SW Flank. No patch.

results.correct_value: ~12,000 ft cumulative gain and loss: day 1 gain 3,550; day 2 gain/loss 8,450; day 3 loss 3,550
results.evidence: A documented 3-day ascent of this exact line (Thornton Pass knob camp, Triumph Pass, Lake Regret, Upper Despair Lake, SE face) records 24 miles and 12,000 ft gained and lost. In the row, gain_ft, loss_ft, the itinerary totalNote and the approach prose all say ~12,000 ft. The route's own waypoints disprove the itinerary's day values. Trailhead 2,500 ft to the 6,050 ft camp is already 3,550 ft on day 1, not 3,200. Day 2 runs camp to summit and back over the 4,600 / 5,520 / 4,900 / 5,100 / 7,296 ft points, which needs at least ~5,800 ft each way, not 2,800. The new values make the days sum to the 12,000 ft total. Day 1 takes the waypoint net of 3,550, and day 3's loss mirrors it. Day 2 carries the remainder, with gain equal to loss because it starts and ends at camp.

results.fact: Pitch count vs ROUTE BREAKDOWN rows
results.evidence: The second ROUTE BREAKDOWN row is a section, not a single pitch, and its own notes say 'Several short pitches ... including a vertical dihedral'. So 2 rows fit 3 pitches: a documented ascent roped two short cliff-band pitches plus one summit-crack pitch, 3 in all.

results.fact: Crux grade shown in TECHNICAL STATS vs actual crux difficulty
results.evidence: One documented ascent calls the summit crux a Class 5.0 dihedral. No second independent source rating the standard route was found; other pages say only 'several pitches of climbing on the summit pyramids'. The row also disagrees with itself on whether the 5.0 dihedral is on the standard line: descent_text and approach_variants say modern parties take the Class 3 east ridge and treat the dihedral as a SE-face variant. Changing `grade` (class system) is not justified without two sources.
Every text field says a 60 m or a 70 m rope will do. rope_length_m can hold only one number, and 60 m is one of the two accepted lengths, so the fields do not disagree.
